From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes, Victor Alade
Subject: Question on monthly close - line item

Gabriel, Victor,

Going through the monthly close package, I have a question on the line item for [describe specific line item, e.g., 'Freight & Handling'] in the [month] report. It’s showing a variance that doesn’t align with our forecast, and I need to understand what drove it before I sign off.

Can you both take a look and give me the breakdown — what’s behind the number, and whether we should expect this to carry into next month? I’d like to close this out by end of day Thursday if possible.

Thanks,
Dana

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Question on monthly close - line item

Hi Dana,

Thanks for flagging this. I’ve pulled the details on the Freight & Handling line for the June report and can confirm the variance is driven by a timing item rather than a recurring cost increase.

Specifically, Kestrel received a vendor rebate credit of about $18k that landed after the statements cut off. Per our accrual policy, I’ve rebooked that credit into June, which is what’s creating the variance against forecast. The offsetting accrual was already in place, so this is a reclassification, not a new charge.

I’ve documented the full breakdown in the close folder—including the vendor reference and the accrual journal entry—so you have the audit trail. Victor has been looped in and is aligned.

On whether this carries into next month: no. This is purely a timing/accrual rebook and will not appear in July’s numbers. I don’t expect any residual impact.

I can have the summary note to you by end of day Thursday as requested. If you’d like a quick call to walk through it, just let me know.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes
